primaryHeadline: Target Service Port Unreachable or Closed
technicalRootCause: Network Layer 3 routing succeeded, but the specific transport port on the target host failed to complete a TCP handshake. The remote daemon is stopped, listening on a different port, or blocked by a target host firewall.

observations.details: Active network interface "Wi-Fi" (172.17.48.79/255.255.248.0) connected with Default Gateway 172.17.48.1.
observations.limitations: Interface inspection checks local host configuration only. Having a valid IP and gateway assigned does NOT mean the gateway is actually reachable or providing Internet transit.

observations.details: ICMP ping to 172.17.48.1 succeeded: 3/3 packets received (0% loss), avg RTT 5ms.
observations.limitations: IMPORTANT: A failed ICMP ping does NOT prove a host is down or offline. Many modern operating systems, cloud providers (like AWS/Azure), and edge firewalls intentionally filter ICMP by default while keeping HTTP/HTTPS (ports 80/443) fully operational.

observations.details: TCP connection refused (RST received) by 127.0.0.1:59999. The host is reachable on the network, but no service is listening on port 59999, or a local firewall actively rejected the socket.
observations.limitations: An active connection refusal proves Layer 3 reachability to the target IP, isolating the failure strictly to Layer 4/7 (service port or firewall).

testsFailed: TCP Port 59999 Connection: TCP connection refused (RST received) by 127.0.0.1:59999. The host is reachable on the network, but no service is listening on port 59999, or a local firewall actively rejected the socket.
alternativeExplanations: An intermediate stateful firewall or cloud security group (e.g. AWS Security Group / iptables) may be dropping inbound connections on this port.
If an active TCP RST was returned (ECONNREFUSED), the operating system on the destination is alive and rejecting the socket connection.
recommendedSteps: Verify whether the server process (e.g., Apache, Nginx, Node.js) is running on the target machine.
Check server-side firewall rules (iptables, UFW, Windows Defender Firewall).
Verify listening sockets on target host using "netstat -an" or "ss -tulpn".
report.limitationsStatement: Evidence-based diagnosis is constrained by observable responses and ICMP/TCP protocol semantics. Intermediate stateful firewalls, packet filters, and cloud policies can mimic or mask network outages.
